{{Quote|One of the aiwha saw that the god-beast had exposed his soft throat, and sacrificing himself, charged and clamped down hard with his jaws.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="tale" />}}
According to a [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod|legend]], an '''aiwha''' [[Death/Legends|sacrificed]] himself to save his [[Unidentified aiwha pod|pod]] when the [[Deity/Legends|god-beast]] [[Protas]] stopped the [[Pod (social group)|pod]] from traveling south for the [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] [[Winter/Legends|winter]]. Knowing they would die if they returned north, the [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] pod [[Destruction of Protas|fought]] Protas. The pod struggled to overcome their enemy until Protas exposed his throat, which the male aiwha saw and clamped down upon. Protas attempted to dislodge the aiwha, beating at and killing the aiwha. Even in death, the aiwha's jaws did not release, allowing his pod to deal a final blow to the god-beast.

==Biography==
===Of a god-beast&hellip;===
{{Quote|You cannot pass. Go back to the north seas and freeze.''"<br />"''Why, Master Protas?''"<br />"''Because it pleases me.|Protas and the aiwha pod, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="tale" />}}
[[File:Kamino.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The planet Kamino, home of the mythical aiwha and his pod]]
According to the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Species/Legends|species]]' mythological tale "[[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod]]," an [[Aiwha/Legends|aiwha]] lived with his [[Unidentified aiwha pod|pod]] in the [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] of<ref name="tale" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. One [[Winter/Legends|winter]], the [[Pod (social group)|pod]] was traveling south out of the [[Temperature/Legends|cold]] northern [[Water/Legends|waters]] when they encountered the [[Deity/Legends|god-beast]] [[Protas]], ruler of Kamino's oceans as the most powerful beast.<ref name="tale" />

Previously, Protas was said to have [[Battle of Thalina|defeated]] the titan [[Melkorr]] and [[Battle of the Ancient Trench|overcome]] an army of [[kikla]] swimmers, both of whom had challenged the [[Magic/Legends|mystical]] Protas for his authority and rule. With the victories over his challengers, Protas became arrogant in his old age. It was with that mindset that he prevented the aiwha pod from continuing their journey south, directing them to turn back north on a whim.<ref name="tale" />

===&hellip;and aiwha===
{{Quote|But being aiwha, and not desirous of glory and fame, they did not announce their challenge to Protas in the manner of the old ways. Instead, they simply and swiftly, attacked.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="tale" />}}
Knowing they would [[Death/Legends|die]] if they returned to the northern waters, the aiwha allegedly [[Destruction of Protas|attacked]] Protas as a unified force without warning or any desire for either fame or glory. Despite swarming the monster-god and making powerful attacks, they could not break the defenses of Protas' thick skin with enough efficacy to deal a killing blow. In the midst of the battle, Protas exposed his soft throat, creating an opening. The male aiwha saw the vulnerability and took advantage, clamping down on Protas' throat with his jaws. Realizing his error, Protas fought against the aiwha, dealing blow after blow to the brave creature. The blows took their toll, killing the aiwha but without complete success&mdash;even in death the aiwha did not release Protas, allowing the pod to deal a final blow and ending the battle.<ref name="tale" />

The apparent sacrifice made by the aiwha, which allowed his pod to achieve victory, was remembered and immortalized in the tale that would eventually be translated from [[Kaminoan (language)/Legends|Kaminoan]] into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] by an individual named [[Ryan Kaufman]]. The conduct of the pod in defeating Protas without seeking glory or power; the resulting peace in Protas' absence; and the self-sacrifice of the male aiwha, explained why the aiwha were accorded the respect of all the creatures of Kamino.<ref name="tale" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|But even in death, the brave aiwha hung on, never letting go, to allow his friends to strike at Protas a final time.|Ryan Kaufman, "The Tale of the Aiwha Pod"|<ref name="tale" />}}
The aiwha, like the rest of his pod, did not seek glory or fame and took to battle out of his necessity to survive. He was brave and cared deeply for his pod, sacrificing himself to ensure their survival.<ref name="tale" />

==Skills and abilities==
The aiwha was observant, noticing the weakness shown by Protas in the midst of battle. He also had strong jaws, able to hold on to Protas despite the beating sustained by the god-beast.<ref name="tale" />

==Behind the scenes==
The aiwha appeared in "[[The Tale of the Aiwha Pod (short story)|The Tale of the Aiwha Pod]]," a [[List of short stories|short story]] by [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman]], which was published in the [[2005]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando: Prima Official Game Guide]]''.<ref name="tale" />
